markets.name: Plac Wolności Christmas Market (Betlejem Poznańskie)
markets.bestTime: 5:00 PM - 7:30 PM (Ferris wheel illuminations & stage performances)
markets.specialty: St. Martin's Croissants, artisan ceramics, and giant illuminated ferris wheel
markets.details: The centerpiece of Betlejem Poznańskie featuring over 60 wooden stalls, an open-air ice rink, an illuminated ferris wheel, and holiday stages.
markets.description: Set on Poznań's grand public square, Betlejem Poznańskie on Plac Wolności features an illuminated 33-meter ferris wheel, authentic wooden stalls, hot mulled wine in commemorative boot mugs, and fresh Rogale Świętomarcińskie.
mustTry: Grzaniec z Wiśniówką (Mulled Wine w/ Cherry)
Smażone Pierogi z Kapustą i Grzybami

markets.name: Stary Rynek Old Market Square Fair
markets.bestTime: 11:45 AM (Daily Town Hall Goat Clashing) & 6:00 PM (Dusk glow)
markets.specialty: Historic Renaissance backdrop & international ice sculpture displays
markets.details: Surrounding the iconic 16th-century Renaissance Town Hall, this historic fair hosts the annual International Ice Sculpture Festival and regional Wielkopolska crafts.
markets.description: Framed by colorful merchant houses and the Renaissance Town Hall, Stary Rynek is the cultural heart of Poznań festivities with live woodcarvers, ice sculptors, and regional folk choirs.
highlights: Renaissance Town Hall & Goat Clock Tower Backdrop
Regional Greater Poland Smoked Meats & Cheeses
mustTry: Gzik Wielkopolski z Pyrami (Cottage Cheese & Baked Potatoes)

markets.name: Międzynarodowe Targi Poznańskie (MTP) Winter Fair
markets.specialty: Indoor-outdoor winter wonderland with massive light installations
markets.details: A contemporary winter fair hosted at Poland’s premier exhibition grounds featuring illuminated light labyrinths, indoor artisan gift halls, and gourmet culinary pavilions.
markets.description: MTP Winter Fair transforms the historic trade fair grounds with thousands of twinkling LEDs, covered winter artisan pavilions, food trucks, and interactive family activities.
mustTry: Gourmet Belgian Waffles with Plum Jam

mustSee.name: Poznań Town Hall (Ratusz) & Mechanical Goats
mustSee.title: Poznań Town Hall (Ratusz) & Mechanical Goats
mustSee.description: One of Northern Europe's most magnificent Renaissance civic buildings designed by Giovanni Battista di Quadro. Every day at 12:00 noon (and 3:00 PM), two mechanical metal billy goats emerge above the clock tower to butt heads 12 times.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Located in the center of Stary Rynek (Old Market Square).
mustSee.pricing: Square free; Town Hall Museum ~15 PLN (~$4.00 USD)

mustSee.name: Ostrów Tumski & Poznań Cathedral of SS. Peter and Paul
mustSee.title: Ostrów Tumski & Poznań Cathedral of SS. Peter and Paul
mustSee.description: The ancient island cradle where Poland began in 966 AD. Inside Poland’s oldest cathedral, the Golden Chapel holds the royal sarcophagi of Poland’s first rulers: Duke Mieszko I and King Bolesław the Brave.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 15-min walk east from Old Town or Tram 3, 4, 8 to Katedra stop.
mustSee.pricing: Cathedral free; Crypt & Royal Tombs ~10 PLN (~$2.65 USD)
mustSee.openTimes: Daily 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM (except during religious services)

mustSee.name: Imperial Castle (Zamek Cesarski)
mustSee.title: Imperial Castle (Zamek Cesarski)
mustSee.description: The last imperial palace built in Europe (1910) for German Emperor Wilhelm II, later redesigned during WWII and now thriving as Poznań's vibrant cultural center with galleries, cinema, and winter courtyards.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 10-min walk west of Plac Wolności or Tram 2, 5, 13 to Zamek stop.
mustSee.pricing: Castle courtyards free; Exhibitions ~15–20 PLN (~$4.00–$5.35 USD)

mustSee.name: Rogalowe Muzeum Poznania (Croissant Museum)
mustSee.title: Rogalowe Muzeum Poznania (Croissant Museum)
mustSee.description: An interactive comedy and culinary show housed in a Renaissance townhouse overlooking the Town Hall. Learn the secret recipe and legend of St. Martin’s croissants and earn an apprentice baker certificate.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Located on Stary Rynek directly opposite the Town Hall.
mustSee.pricing: 32–38 PLN (~$8.50–$10.00 USD) incl. fresh croissant tasting
mustSee.openTimes: Shows run daily (English sessions available at 2:00 PM; reserve online)

mustSee.name: Citadel Park (Park Cytadela) & Fort Winiary
mustSee.title: Citadel Park (Park Cytadela) & Fort Winiary
mustSee.description: A 100-hectare park built upon the ruins of Prussia's massive 19th-century Fort Winiary. Features Magdalena Abakanowicz's monumental iron sculpture installation 'The Unrecognized' (Nierozpoznani) and military history museums.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Tram 3, 4, 10 to Garbary or Armii Poznań stop (~10 mins from Old Town).
mustSee.pricing: Park grounds free; Military museums ~12 PLN (~$3.20 USD)
mustSee.openTimes: Park open 24/7; Museums Tue-Sun 10:00 AM - 4:00 PM

mustSee.name: Poznań Fara Church (St. Stanislaus Basilica)
mustSee.title: Poznań Fara Church (St. Stanislaus Basilica)
mustSee.description: One of Central Europe’s most breathtaking High Baroque basilicas, boasting towering pink marbleized columns, gilded altars, and a legendary 19th-century organ built by Friedrich Ladegast.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 2-min walk south from Stary Rynek along Świętosławska street.
mustSee.pricing: Free entry (donations appreciated); Organ concerts free/donation
mustSee.openTimes: Mon-Sat 6:30 AM - 7:30 PM, Sun 7:00 AM - 8:30 PM

mustSee.name: Poznań Old Town & Croissant Tasting Guided Walking Tour
mustSee.title: Poznań Old Town & Croissant Tasting Guided Walking Tour
mustSee.description: Immersive 2.5-hour walking tour covering the Renaissance Stary Rynek, goat legends, Baroque Fara, Ostrów Tumski birthplace of Poland, and a warm St. Martin croissant and coffee tasting.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Departs from the Bamberka Fountain on Stary Rynek.
mustSee.pricing: 70–90 PLN (~$18.50–$24.00 USD) per person

restaurantsDetailed.name: Brovaria Hotel & Microbrewery
restaurantsDetailed.signature: House Pilsner & Honey Beer, Braised Pork Knuckle, Roasted Duck with Dumplings (Pyzy)
restaurantsDetailed.description: Award-winning microbrewery on the Market Square where copper brewing vats gleam behind dining tables, serving fresh unfiltered beer and hearty Wielkopolska classics.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Restauracja Bamberka
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Poznań Duck with Red Cabbage & Steamed Pyzy, Czernina Soup, Baked Zander
restaurantsDetailed.description: Tribute restaurant honoring the 18th-century German Bambrzy settlers who shaped Poznań folklore, offering warm authentic dining beside the famous Bamberka fountain.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Wiejskie Jadło Poznań
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Żurek in Sourdough Bread Loaf, Bigos Myśliwski, Pan-Fried Ruskie Pierogi
restaurantsDetailed.description: Cozy folk-art interior with painted timbers and clay pottery, specializing in comforting traditional home-cooked Polish recipes and warm mulled ciders.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Pierogarnia Stary Młyn Poznań
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Oven-Baked Piecuchy with Smoked Bacon, Boiled Wild Forest Mushroom Pierogi
restaurantsDetailed.description: Acclaimed dumpling specialist renowned for traditional boiled pierogi and giant crispy oven-baked crusty piecuchy stuffed with savory meats and cheeses.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Restauracja Muga (1 Michelin Star)
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Seasonal Tasting Menu with Regional Foraged Ingredients, Sommelier Wine Pairings
restaurantsDetailed.description: Poznań's first Michelin-starred culinary gem offering an unforgettable sensory journey of refined modern European gastronomy curated by Chef Artur Skotarczyk.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Pijalnia Wódki i Piwa Poznań
restaurantsDetailed.cuisine: Retro Polish PRL Tapas & Infused Vodka Shots
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Chili-Lemon & Salted Caramel Vodka Shots, Pickled Herring (Śledź), Steak Tartare
restaurantsDetailed.description: Vibrant retro 1960s Polish PRL bar serving budget-friendly ice-cold vodka shots and classic drinking appetizers on bustling Wrocławska street.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Ministerstwo Browaru Taproom
restaurantsDetailed.cuisine: Polish Craft Beer on Tap & Bar Snacks
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Rotating 16 Polish Craft Draft Taps (IPAs, Baltic Porters, Sours), Warm Pretzels
restaurantsDetailed.description: A temple for Polish craft beer enthusiasts with sixteen continuously rotating artisanal taps from top Polish microbreweries and a lively cellar atmosphere.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Kawiarnia Stonewall
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Single-Origin Aeropress Brews, Vegan Cheesecake, Hot Spiced Winter Latte
restaurantsDetailed.description: A welcoming, inclusive community café run by Grupa Stonewall where 100% of proceeds support local equality initiatives, serving top-tier specialty coffee and artisan cakes.

markets.name: Rynek Staromiejski Medieval Christmas Market
markets.hours: Mon-Thu 12:00 PM - 9:00 PM, Fri 12:00 PM - 10:00 PM, Sat 10:00 AM - 10:00 PM, Sun 10:00 AM - 9:00 PM
markets.bestTime: 4:30 PM - 7:00 PM (Gothic Town Hall illumination & gingerbread aromas)
markets.specialty: Authentic 700-year-old Toruń gingerbread, spiced honey wines, and Gothic square ambiance
markets.details: Nestled beneath the towering red-brick 13th-century Town Hall and Copernicus Monument, Toruń’s Christmas Market is famous for world-renowned spiced gingerbread and warm medieval charm.
markets.description: Enclosed by intact 13th-century brick Gothic townhouses, Toruń's market fills the medieval square with festive wooden chalets, glowing arches, master gingerbread bakers, and live highlander carolers.
highlights: Hot Spiced Toruń Honey Mead (Miód Toruński)
mustTry: Toruńskie Pierniki z Powidłami (Plum Jam Spiced Gingerbread)
Grzany Miód Toruński (Hot Toruń Spiced Mead)

markets.name: Rynek Nowomiejski Craft & Artisan Fair
markets.bestTime: 3:00 PM - 6:00 PM (Quiet artisan shopping & local bakery stalls)
markets.specialty: Handcrafted toys, beeswax goods, and local Kuyavian craft foods
markets.details: A quieter, charming sister market set in the New Town Market Square centered around master woodturners, organic beekeepers, and regional Kuyavian bakers.
markets.description: Set on the octagonal New Town Square, this market offers an intimate, relaxed stroll focused on small-batch beekeepers, hand-loomed winter scarves, and local organic delicacies.
mustTry: Hot Mulled Cider with Cloves and Cinnamon

mustSee.name: Old Town Hall & Copernicus Monument (Ratusz Staromiejski)
mustSee.title: Old Town Hall & Copernicus Monument (Ratusz Staromiejski)
mustSee.description: One of the largest and most intact Gothic brick town halls in Europe, built between 1391 and 1399. Climb the 40-meter tower for a panoramic view over the red-tiled medieval roofs and Vistula River.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Center of Rynek Staromiejski (Old Market Square).
mustSee.pricing: Museum entry ~18 PLN (~$4.80 USD); Tower climb ~15 PLN (~$4.00 USD)

mustSee.name: Living Museum of Gingerbread (Żywe Muzeum Piernika)
mustSee.title: Living Museum of Gingerbread (Żywe Muzeum Piernika)
mustSee.description: An extraordinary 16th-century living bakery museum where Master Bakers guide visitors through crushing spices, kneading honey dough into wooden molds, and baking authentic Toruń gingerbread to take home.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 3-min walk south of Rynek Staromiejski on Rabiańska street.
mustSee.pricing: 34–39 PLN (~$9.00–$10.50 USD) incl. hands-on baking workshop
mustSee.openTimes: Daily 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM (English shows run at 1:00 PM & 4:00 PM; advance booking advised)

mustSee.name: Nicolaus Copernicus House (Dom Mikołaja Kopernika)
mustSee.title: Nicolaus Copernicus House (Dom Mikołaja Kopernika)
mustSee.description: The reconstructed 15th-century Gothic patrician townhouse where Nicolaus Copernicus was born in 1473. Interactive multimedia exhibits explore his astronomical breakthroughs, medieval trade, and Renaissance instruments.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 3-min walk southwest from Rynek Staromiejski along Kopernika street.

mustSee.name: The Leaning Tower of Toruń (Krzywa Wieża)
mustSee.title: The Leaning Tower of Toruń (Krzywa Wieża)
mustSee.location: Krzywa Wieża, Pod Krzywą Wieżą 1, 87-100 Toruń, Poland
mustSee.description: A 14th-century Gothic defensive tower tilting 1.46 meters off vertical. According to medieval legend, visitors test their honesty by standing with their heels and back against the wall without toppling forward.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 5-min walk west of Rynek Staromiejski along the defensive city walls.
mustSee.pricing: Exterior free; Interior exhibition ~10 PLN (~$2.65 USD)

mustSee.name: Teutonic Castle Ruins (Zamek Krzyżacki)
mustSee.title: Teutonic Castle Ruins (Zamek Krzyżacki)
mustSee.description: The horseshoe-shaped brick ruins of the 13th-century Teutonic Knights' fortress, demolished by rebellious Toruń townspeople in 1454 during the Thirteen Years' War to assert civic freedom.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 5-min walk east from Rynek Staromiejski along Szeroka and Przedzamcze.
mustSee.pricing: 15 PLN (~$4.00 USD) for castle grounds and subterranean vaults

mustSee.name: Cathedral of SS. John the Baptist and John the Evangelist
mustSee.title: Cathedral of SS. John the Baptist and John the Evangelist
mustSee.description: Monumental 13th-century Gothic cathedral housing the original 13th-century font where Copernicus was baptized, as well as the famous 7-ton 'Tuba Dei' (God's Trumpet) bell cast in 1500.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 2-min walk south from Rynek Staromiejski on Żeglarska street.
mustSee.pricing: Free entry to cathedral; Bell tower climb ~12 PLN (~$3.20 USD)
mustSee.openTimes: Mon-Sat 9:00 AM - 5:00 PM, Sun 12:30 PM - 5:30 PM

mustSee.name: Toruń UNESCO Medieval Gothic & Pierniki Guided Walking Tour
mustSee.title: Toruń UNESCO Medieval Gothic & Pierniki Guided Walking Tour
mustSee.description: Delightful 2-hour guided walking tour exploring the undamaged UNESCO medieval center, Copernicus birthplace, the Leaning Tower, and historic gingerbread bakeries.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Departs from the Nicolaus Copernicus Monument in Rynek Staromiejski.
mustSee.pricing: 60–80 PLN (~$16.00–$21.50 USD) per person

restaurants: Karczma Spichrz (18th Century Historic Granary Dining)
Jan Olbracht Browar Staromiejski (Royal Craft Brewery)

restaurantsDetailed.name: Karczma Spichrz
restaurantsDetailed.cuisine: Authentic Kuyavian & Old Polish Hearth Cooking
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Roasted Pork Ribs in Gingerbread Glaze, Duck with Apples, Hunter’s Bigos in Loaf
restaurantsDetailed.description: Set inside a monumental 18th-century timber-framed granary by the river gate, serving hearty Polish delicacies cooked over open charcoal hearths.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Restauracja Manekin Toruń
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Baked Crepes with Chanterelles and Chicken, Sweet Cottage Cheese & Pierniki Crepe
restaurantsDetailed.description: The original flagship birthplace of Poland's beloved Manekin creperie chain, serving over 50 varieties of oversized savory and dessert crepes at incredible value.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Restauracja Pod Aniołem
restaurantsDetailed.cuisine: Royal Polish & Toruń Gingerbread Infused Specialties
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Venison Stew in Bread Bowl, Roast Duck in Honey-Spice Sauce, Homemade Pierogi
restaurantsDetailed.description: Atmospheric restaurant nestled in the 14th-century brick cellar vaults beneath Toruń Town Hall, renowned for traditional game recipes and candlelit romance.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Pierogarnia Stary Toruń
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Oven-Baked Piecuchy with Smoked Meat, Boiled Ruskie Pierogi with Fried Onions
restaurantsDetailed.description: Charming medieval-themed dumpling tavern famous for giant oven-baked crusty pierogi with rich garlic dipping sauce and hearty winter soups.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Restauracja Szeroka No 9
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Sous-vide Deer Loin, Wild Sea Trout with Herbal Risotto, Artisanal Dessert Selection
restaurantsDetailed.description: Elegant fine dining on Toruń's central pedestrian boulevard, marrying regional Vistula ingredients with contemporary culinary flair and an extensive wine cellar.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Jan Olbracht Browar Staromiejski
restaurantsDetailed.address: Jan Olbracht Browar Staromiejski, Szczytna 15, 87-100 Toruń, Poland
restaurantsDetailed.cuisine: Artisan Craft Beer & Polish Tavern Fare
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Piernikowe Dark Gingerbread Beer, Olbracht Pilsner, Crispy Golonka Pork Knuckle
restaurantsDetailed.description: Toruń's premier craft brewery named after King Jan Olbracht, brewing unique seasonal beers including the city's signature dark spiced Piernikowe gingerbread beer.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Kawiarnia Lenkiewicz
restaurantsDetailed.cuisine: Artisan Ice Cream, Pastries & Specialty Coffee
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Signature Piernik Cake, Artisan Hot Chocolate with Cinnamon, Handcrafted Ice Cream
restaurantsDetailed.description: Beloved Toruń confectionery institution founded in 1945, world-famous for irresistible cakes, hot chocolates, and freshly baked pastries right on the Market Square.

markets.name: Targ Węglowy Main Christmas Market (Jarmark Bożonarodzeniowy)
markets.hours: Sun-Thu 12:00 PM - 8:00 PM, Fri-Sat 12:00 PM - 9:00 PM (Closed Dec 24/25)
markets.bestTime: 5:00 PM - 7:30 PM (Lucek the Moose speeches & carousel lights)
markets.specialty: Talking Moose Lucek, 3-story Advent Pyramid, and Baltic Amber gifts
markets.details: Voted among the best European Christmas Markets, Gdańsk's fair features romantic Venetian carousels, an illuminated talking moose animatronic, and hundreds of Hanseatic chalets.
markets.description: Set against the historic Prison Tower and Great Armoury, Gdańsk's Christmas Market charms visitors with the animatronic Lucek the Moose, glowing Venetian carousel, steaming Grzaniec Gdański in boot mugs, and artisan Baltic amber craftsmen.
mustTry: Grzaniec Gdański z Imbirem (Spiced Ginger Mulled Wine)
Smażone Ryby Bałtyckie (Fried Baltic Fish Bites)
Pieczone Kasztany i Oscypek (Roasted Chestnuts & Grilled Cheese)

markets.name: Ulica Tkacka & Zbrojownia Artisans Fair
markets.bestTime: 4:00 PM - 6:30 PM (Fine jewelry browsing & hot mead tastings)
markets.specialty: High-end Polish design, fine Baltic amber art, and artisanal honey wine
markets.details: An artisan extension extending past the Great Armoury along Tkacka street, featuring curated Polish fashion designers, jewelers, and craft spirits.
markets.description: Radiating from the Renaissance Great Armoury, this boutique pedestrian lane offers refined shopping for Baltic amber artists, hand-loomed woolens, and warm spice liqueurs.

markets.name: Granary Island (Wyspa Spichrzów) Winter Promenade
markets.bestTime: 6:00 PM - 9:00 PM (Riverfront light reflections & cocktail lounges)
markets.specialty: Modern waterfront winter dining, illuminated footbridges, and AmberSky wheel
markets.details: Gdańsk’s buzzing waterfront entertainment district glowing with winter light displays, outdoor fire lounges, and waterside views of the historic Old Crane.
markets.description: Connecting to Old Town via illuminated footbridges across the Motława River, Granary Island offers vibrant outdoor heaters, riverside craft bars, and festive winter energy.
highlights: Heated Outdoor Fire Pits & Winter Lounges
Waterside Views of the Medieval Crane (Żuraw)
mustTry: Warm Belgian Hot Chocolate with Rum

mustSee.name: Long Market & Main Town Hall (Długi Targ & Ratusz)
mustSee.title: Long Market & Main Town Hall (Długi Targ & Ratusz)
mustSee.description: The breathtaking heart of the Royal Way (Droga Królewska) lined with Dutch Mannerist merchant townhouses, Artus Court, and the 83-meter Gothic tower of the Main Town Hall.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Central pedestrian axis of Główne Miasto (Main Town).
mustSee.pricing: Square free; Town Hall Museum ~16 PLN (~$4.25 USD)

mustSee.name: Neptune's Fountain (Fontanna Neptuna)
mustSee.title: Neptune's Fountain (Fontanna Neptuna)
mustSee.description: The 17th-century bronze fountain of the Roman sea god holding his trident in front of Artus Court. Legend says Neptune struck his trident to shatter golden coins into the golden flakes of Danziger Goldwasser liqueur.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Located in Długi Targ right in front of Artus Court.
mustSee.pricing: Free

mustSee.name: St. Mary's Basilica (Bazylika Mariacka)
mustSee.title: St. Mary's Basilica (Bazylika Mariacka)
mustSee.description: The largest brick church in the world, capable of holding 25,000 worshippers. Features a monumental 15th-century astronomical clock by Hans Düringer and a 400-step tower with staggering Baltic views.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 3-min walk north from Długi Targ along Piwna or Kramarska street.
mustSee.pricing: Church free; Tower climb ~14 PLN (~$3.75 USD)
mustSee.openTimes: Mon-Sat 8:30 AM - 5:30 PM, Sun 11:00 AM - 5:30 PM

mustSee.name: Motława Waterfront & Medieval Port Crane (Żuraw Gdański)
mustSee.title: Motława Waterfront & Medieval Port Crane (Żuraw Gdański)
mustSee.description: The 15th-century double-towered wooden harbor crane on the Motława River, once the largest in medieval Europe. Used to load grain and step ship masts using massive human-powered treadwheels.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Walk along the river promenade (Długie Pobrzeże) from Green Gate.
mustSee.pricing: Promenade free; National Maritime Museum interior ~18 PLN (~$4.80 USD)

mustSee.name: Museum of the Second World War (Muzeum II Wojny Światowej)
mustSee.title: Museum of the Second World War (Muzeum II Wojny Światowej)
mustSee.description: A world-renowned museum housed inside a dramatic tilted architectural landmark. The underground exhibition presents an unforgettable, comprehensive chronicle of the civilian and military experience of WWII.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 12-min walk north along Motława River or Bus 100/130 to Muzeum stop.
mustSee.pricing: 29 PLN (~$7.75 USD) (Advance ticket booking strongly recommended)

mustSee.name: European Solidarity Centre (Europejskie Centrum Solidarności)
mustSee.title: European Solidarity Centre (Europejskie Centrum Solidarności)
mustSee.description: Clad in rusted shipyard steel by the historic Gate No. 2 of the Gdańsk Shipyard, this award-winning museum tells the inspiring story of Lech Wałęsa, Solidarność, and the peaceful collapse of European communism.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 10-min walk from Gdańsk Główny station or Tram 8, 10 to Plac Solidarności.
mustSee.pricing: 30 PLN (~$8.00 USD) incl. excellent audio guide
mustSee.openTimes: Mon, Wed-Fri 10:00 AM - 5:00 PM; Sat-Sun 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM (Tue closed)

mustSee.name: Amber Museum at Great Mill (Muzeum Bursztynu - Wielki Młyn)
mustSee.title: Amber Museum at Great Mill (Muzeum Bursztynu - Wielki Młyn)
mustSee.location: Wielki Młyn, Wielkie Młyny 16, 80-849 Gdańsk, Poland
mustSee.description: Housed inside Europe’s largest medieval watermill (Wielki Młyn), showcasing prehistoric plant and animal inclusions in amber, royal guild jewelry, and contemporary Baltic amber artwork.
mustSee.howToGetThere: 5-min walk south of Gdańsk Główny station near St. Catherine Church.

mustSee.name: Gdańsk Old Town, Hanseatic Amber & Solidarity Guided Walking Tour
mustSee.title: Gdańsk Old Town, Hanseatic Amber & Solidarity Guided Walking Tour
mustSee.description: Top-rated 2.5-hour tour covering the Royal Way, Neptune’s Fountain, St. Mary’s Basilica, amber workshops on picturesque Mariacka Street, and the Motława waterfront crane.
mustSee.howToGetThere: Departs from Neptune’s Fountain on Długi Targ.
mustSee.pricing: 75–95 PLN (~$20.00–$25.50 USD) per person

restaurants: Restauracja Kubicki (Oldest Surviving Gdańsk Dining since 1918)
Gdański Bowke (Maritime Port Fare & Polish Craft Beer)
Bar Mleczny Neptun (Authentic Historic Milk Bar on Długa)

restaurantsDetailed.name: Pierogarnia Mandu Centrum
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Pan-Fried Duck & Cranberry Pierogi, Traditional Ruskie, Sweet Blueberry Dumplings
restaurantsDetailed.description: Gdańsk's premier pierogi destination where master cooks hand-roll, stuff, and boil fresh dumplings behind an open glass kitchen. Incredibly popular, warm, and delicious.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Restauracja Kubicki
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Crispy Pork Knuckle in Beer Glaze, Pan-Seared Baltic Salmon, Hunter’s Wild Boar Stew
restaurantsDetailed.description: Gdańsk's oldest operating restaurant (since 1918) overlooking the Motława River, maintaining pre-war elegance, live piano melodies, and exquisite traditional Polish game and seafood.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Gdański Bowke
restaurantsDetailed.address: Karczma Piwna "Gdański Bowke", Długie Pobrzeże 11, 80-888 Gdańsk, Poland
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Danziger Goldwasser, Herring in Mustard-Cream Sauce, Roast Goose Leg with Red Cabbage
restaurantsDetailed.description: Vibrant maritime tavern on the Motława promenade themed around 19th-century port life, serving authentic Kashubian recipes, freshly baked sourdough, and house liqueurs.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Brovarnia Gdańsk
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Award-Winning Złoto Brovarni Pilsner, Dark Smoked Bock, Braised Beef Cheeks
restaurantsDetailed.description: Celebrated microbrewery inside a restored 17th-century granary overlooking Gdańsk Marina, renowned for world-class craft beers and refined Polish cuisine.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Bar Mleczny Neptun
restaurantsDetailed.cuisine: Authentic Traditional Polish Milk Bar Fare
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Kompocik, Kotlet Schabowy with Potatoes, Pomidorowa Tomato Soup with Noodles
restaurantsDetailed.description: A genuine, beloved Polish milk bar operating on picturesque Długa street since 1958, serving fast, honest, comforting home-cooked meals at unbeatable budget prices.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Restauracja Fino Gdańsk
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Seasonal Degustation Tasting Menu, Halibut with Sea Buckthorn, Wild Venison Tartare
restaurantsDetailed.description: Intimate, critically acclaimed culinary sanctuary in the heart of Old Town celebrating seasonal Baltic ingredients with innovative textures and delicate plating.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Wiśniewski Cherry Liqueur House
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Hot Spiced Wiśniówka Liqueur in Stemware, Chilled Cherry Cordials, Dark Chocolates
restaurantsDetailed.description: Cult boutique bar dedicated to Poland’s finest artisanal cherry liqueur (Wiśniówka), served steaming hot in crystal glasses on atmospheric Piwna street.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Pub Pułapka Craft Beer
restaurantsDetailed.cuisine: Polish Independent Craft Beer on Tap
restaurantsDetailed.signature: 12 Rotating Polish Craft Taps (Baltic Porters, NEIPAs), Artisanal Cider, Jerky
restaurantsDetailed.description: Legendary indie craft beer bar favored by locals and travelers alike, featuring an ever-changing chalkboard of Poland’s top microbreweries and relaxed industrial vibes.

restaurantsDetailed.name: Drukarnia Café
restaurantsDetailed.signature: Pour-Over V60 Brews, Avocado Sourdough Toast, Homemade Warm Cinnamon Buns
restaurantsDetailed.description: Iconic specialty coffee sanctuary located on cobblestone Mariacka street lined with gargoyle rainspouts, serving exceptional filter coffees and delicious morning toasts.
